questions.question: What is the tenure of the Chairperson of National Human Rights Commission?
questions.solution:
Tenure: The chairman and members hold office for a term of 3 years or until they attain the age of 70 years, whichever is earlier.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

National Human Rights Commission (NHRC) of India ​

 
• It is a statutory body constituted under the Protection of Human Rights Act (PHRA), 1993 on 12 October 1993. 
 
• It is in conformity with the Paris Principles, adopted at the first international workshop on national institutions for the promotion and protection of human rights held in Paris in October 1991, and endorsed by the General Assembly of the United Nations by its Regulations 48/134 of 20 December 1993.
 
• The NHRC is an embodiment of India’s concern for the promotion and protection of human rights.
 
• The Commission is responsible for spreading human rights awareness amongst the masses and encouraging the efforts of all stakeholders in the field of human rights literacy not only at the national level but at the international level too.
 
• The NHRC, India plays an active role in coordinating with other NHRIs of the world to enhance awareness from the perspective of human rights.
 
• The commission has no power to punish the violators of human rights, nor to award any relief including monetary relief to the victim.
 
• The Protection of Human Rights (Amendment) Bill, 2019 amended the Protection of Human Rights Act (PHRA), 1993. Some of the amendments were - 
 
 
• Tenure: Earlier the chairman and members hold office for a term of Five years or until they attain the age of 70 years, whichever is earlier. The Bill reduces the term of office to three years or till the age of seventy years, whichever is earlier. Further, the Act allows for the reappointment of members of the NHRC and SHRCs for a period of five years. The Bill removes the five-year limit for reappointment. 
 
• Composition of NHRC: Under the Act, the chairperson of the NHRC is a person who has been a Chief Justice of the Supreme Court. The Bill amends this to provide that a person who has been Chief Justice of the Supreme Court, or a Judge of the Supreme Court will be the chairperson of the NHRC. 
 
• The Act provides for two persons having knowledge of human rights to be appointed as members of the NHRC. The Bill amends this to allow three members to be appointed, of which at least one will be a woman. 
 
• Under the Act, chairpersons of various commissions such as the National Commission for Scheduled Castes, National Commission for Scheduled Tribes, and National Commission for Women are members of the NHRC. The Bill provides for including the chairpersons of the National Commission for Backward Classes, the National Commission for the Protection of Child Rights, and the Chief Commissioner for Persons with Disabilities as members of the NHRC.

questions.question: Why do atoms and non-polar molecules have no dipole moment?

options.text: Because their electronic charge cloud is asymmetrically distributed
Because their electronic charge cloud is missing
Because their electronic charge cloud is symmetrically distributed
Because their electronic charge cloud is scattered

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Because their Electronic Charge Cloud is symmetrically Distributed__****__.__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Atom and Non-Polar molecules have no dipole moment **because their Electronic Charge cloud is symmetrically distributed.**
 
• Nonpolar bonds occur because there is the difference in electronegativity between two atoms is less than 0.4.
 
• **Non-polar bonds do not have any type of net dipole moment** and are generally formed in compounds where there is a presence of symmetry. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• In chemistry, a dipole refers to **the separation of charges within a molecule between two covalently bonded types of atoms or atoms that share an ionic bond**.
 
• The main difference between polar and dipolar molecules is **polar molecules have two opposite ends with opposite electrical charges, whereas dipolar molecules have only two poles**.

• Magnetic field lines appear to move from the South pole towards the North pole inside a magnet.
 
• Magnetic field lines start from the North pole and end up at the South pole.​

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__ **

• Magnetic field lines are a visual tool used to represent glamorous fields.
 
• The four parcels of glamorous field lines are as follows
 
 
• They're unrestricted and non-stop curves.
 
• They're directed from the north pole outside the attraction towards the south pole of the magnet.
 
• The digression at any point on a field line gives the direction of a glamorous field at that point.
 
• Parallel and equidistant filed lines represent an invariant glamorous field. The earth’s glamorous field in a limited space is invariant.

questions.question: Which of the Sustainable Development Goals set by the United Nations aims to achieve universal health coverage that seeks equal access to health services for all men and women?

questions.question: According to the poverty statistics in India (2011-12), which group has the lowest percentage of population below the poverty line?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Goa and Kerala.__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Poverty statistics in India(2011-12) **Goa and Kerala** have the lowest percentage of Population below the Poverty line.
 
• The percentage of persons below the Poverty Line in 2011-12 has been estimated at **25.7%.**
 
• **In rural areas, 13.7% in urban areas, and 21.9% for the country as a whole**.
 
• **Goa** has the least percentage of people living below the poverty line at 5.09 per cent followed by Kerala (7.05 per cent).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The poverty line is **the minimum amount of money a person needs to fulfil the basic necessities of life, like shelter and food**. 
 
• When families are below the poverty line, they qualify for help from the government.
 
• Poverty is about **not having enough money to meet basic needs including food, clothing and shelter**.
